plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
Maintain a substantial cash buffer for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a potential target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and lowering concentration.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to small allocations to reduce overall risk.
Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Add ERX, a strong scanner long setup, to diversify and capture growth.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets risk-first growth, aiming for ~2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality long setup, offering a more stable growth profile.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Increase exposure to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to press growth.
Buy ERX, a strong scanner long setup, to further amplify potential returns.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to target aggressive growth, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by leaning into leverage and concentration. This approach significantly increases both potential upside and drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs are subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to near zero.
Increase QQQI allocation to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on generating reliable income with low drawdown.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: This income plan aims for ~1% per month by prioritizing steady distributions and low drawdown. While it seeks reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
